newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, October 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday, October 18.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Secessionist Northern League party leader Umberto Bossi says his party will participate in the bicameral commission for constitutional reforms (all).

* Brescia magistrate Fabio Salamone, who was the prosecutor in a trial on an alleged plot against former magistrate and Public works minister Antonio Di Pietro, was removed from the case. Newspapers reported that Salamone felt strong personal animosity towards Di Pietro (all)
* The government is expected to name today the new heads of secret services (all).

* After a private meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, prime minister Romano Prodi says the lira will rejoin the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) and that Germany "has no interest in keeping Italy out of Emu" (all).

* Chemist trade unions cancelled their announced protest against the 1997 budget: they had threatened to charge consumers the full price of drugs which are normally paid for by the national health system (all).
* Metalworkers confirmed a national strike on November 15th, but talks over their contract renewal resumes with employers (all).
* The Freedom Alliance wants to present 700 amendments to the 1997 budget, the Northern League party threatens to propose 2.000.

* Olivetti shares rose by 1.21 percent on reports of Mediaset being interested in the mobile phone consortium Omnitel, which Olivetti controls. Mediaset issued a denial. Meanwhile Olivetti is said to be in talks with Taiwanese computer company Acer for the sale of its ailing pc division (MF).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
